title: The New Monarchs: Catastrophe as Opportunity
author: Graham Peebles
content:
In our deluded world one of the perks of huge wealth is power, political and
corporate — and the two are bedmates. Piles of money also ~~seems~~ [seem] to
rot the brain, eroding any semblance of rational thinking and common sense as
the fingers of narcissism and megalomania engulf the mind and poison the soul.

I recently watched a BBC documentary
[entitled](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ID8rMCfm9rA) 'The Tech Billionaire
Takeover'. It featured a series of extremely rich, completely whacky, and very
dangerous characters: playing a central role is Justin Sun, CEO of
[Tron,](https://tron.network) a blockchain platform where crypto can be bought
and sold. Sun is in business with World Liberty Financial, the Trump family
crypto [business](https://worldlibertyfinancial.com), although they seem to
have fallen out and he is now suing them, and, true to form, the Trumps are
suing him. And while the world burns and the people cry out, the pantomime of
money goes on, and on.

Another leading figure in the documentary is Tim Draper — "The Risk Master of
Silicon Valley". A venture capitalist, he
[heads](https://draperuniversity.com/program_hero) up Draper University —
"Building the Next Generation of Superheroes". A weird place where the 'gods
of money and success' form the altarpiece, offering "an intensive immersive
five-weeks pre-accelerator program" in Hero Training — whatever that is.

Curtis Yarvin, a key [figure](https://www.britannica.com/biography/Curtis-
Yarvin) in shaping the ideology shared by Draper, Sun, Trump, Vance and
others, was also featured.

A far-right political blogger and software engineer, in 2008, under his pen
name Mencius Moldbug, Yarvin posted an online pamphlet
[entitled](https://www.cbc.ca/lite/story/9.7032441) _‘Patchwork: A Political
System for the 21st Century’_. The basic idea of 'Patchwork', according to
Moldbug/Yarvin, is the replacement of governments by "a global spiderweb of
tens, even hundreds, of thousands of sovereign mini-countries, each governed
by its own joint-stock corporation without regard to the residents' opinions."
Micro-nations, like [Liberland](https://liberland.org), which was featured in
the BBC programme.

These small island territories, independently governed backwaters, exist
outside international law, with no democratic structures, and are funded not
through taxation — nobody pays tax in such bubbles — but through corporate
donors. Democracy is jettisoned in favour of a corporate monarchy administered
through blockchain, a hidden world of pulsing dashes and dots — where Sun and
Co. envision elections taking place within years, not decades, or not never.

On top of their hatred of democracy and social justice, these blinded
visionaries hold a dismissive approach towards the environmental emergency.

On this issue too there is broad agreement among the techno-colonialist circle
— a symbiotic delusion that might be
[summed](https://emptywheel.net/2025/05/03/introduction-to-yarvins-formalism/)
up by Yarvin, who regards the environmental crisis as "basically
insignificant" compared to violence, which he considers the only truly
significant problem facing humanity. They do not simply ignore the climate
crisis; they see it as an opportunity — 'Catastrophe as an Opportunity'.

Rising sea levels, unbearable heat, drought, floods and so on, are not
regarded as disasters but rather the chance to "start society afresh" along
ideological lines drawn by the new Monarchs. Non-democratic societies built by
the mega-rich from the wreckage of a world ravaged by climate change and
ecological collapse — caused by the very ideology of greed that such men
champion.

Though not featured, Elon Musk also sits comfortably within the paradigm of
extremism that was on display. He has routinely spread misinformation about
climate change, including dismissing farming's impact on the climate. His
false and incendiary statements often align with fringe viewpoints that fuel
division and downplay the urgency of the climate crisis, leading many to label
him a climate denier.

**Disbelief**

All of this madness was new to me, and I spent most of the time shaking my
head in disbelief. To begin with I thought I'd stumbled on a drama series, so
horrific and far-fetched was the content.

I had never heard of micronations; I was aware of crypto and blockchain, but,
like most people, I had no idea what they really are or how they work. I
suspect I am not alone in my ignorance or confusion. Do those investing in
crypto, or regulating it — is it even properly regulated? — understand it any
better? I doubt it. That, I suspect, is precisely the point.

The digital despots sitting behind such systems profit from collective
ignorance. The more obscure the technology, the more power they hold. They
speak in jargon, promise utopia, and nobody questions them – because nobody
wants to admit they do not understand, and anyway, we all have lives to live.

Where, in such a disturbing dark paradigm, do we find 'the people'? Where is
the accountability, the democratic processes, the aspirational ideals like
equality, freedom and social justice?

Wealth, power, inequality, exploitation: entwined social poisons that destroy
democracy, make social justice impossible, and fuel division and conflict —
constitute the very foundations of the world they want to build.

Clearly these would-be monarchs are not concerned with equality, freedom or
social justice — woke ideals, they may call them. On the contrary, they are
open about their plans to dismantle democracy, establish private kingdoms and
install dictators, oh, and replace money with crypto currencies.

All of this led me to ask myself: what kind of world is it that listens to men
like these, and allows them to wield so much power?

It is a world in crisis, without doubt. By 'world' we mean society, and by
society is meant people. There is no society separate from people; society is
not an abstraction existing outside the men and women who populate it.

'The world' cannot be changed because it does not exist as an independent
form. Rather, it is people who must change — and in changing, accept complete
responsibility, both for the chaos that is all around us, and for the new
world that, if we are to prosper — indeed, if we are to survive — must be
built.

Only then, when we all accept total responsibility for ourselves, for our
neighbour and by extension, for society, and in doing so act for the common
good, the welfare of our neighbour and the natural world, only then can people
like Sun, Draper and 'The Trumps' — divisive, cruel men — be consigned to the
margins. Their ludicrous, dangerous vision of society seen clearly for what it
is, and consigned to irrelevance.

The post [The New Monarchs: Catastrophe as
Opportunity](https://www.counterpunch.org/2026/07/24/the-new-monarchs-
catastrophe-as-opportunity/) appeared first on
[CounterPunch.org](https://www.counterpunch.org).
